# openssl — 2003 high-value CVEs (CVSS>=7, CISA KEV, Exploit-DB, or SSVC exploitation active/poc)

Full records for all 7 openssl CVEs of 2003 are in `data/cve/vendors/openssl/2003.jsonl`.

### CVE-2003-0078
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2004-09-01 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 22264: OpenSSL 0.9.x - CBC Error Information Leakage (remote/linux, 2003-02-19, verified=1)

ssl3_get_record in s3_pkt.c for OpenSSL before 0.9.7a and 0.9.6 before 0.9.6i does not perform a MAC computation if an incorrect block cipher padding is used, which causes an information leak (timing discrepancy) that may make it easier to launch cryptographic attacks that rely on distinguishing between padding and MAC verification errors, possibly leading to extraction of the original plaintext, aka the "Vaudenay timing attack."

Affected:

### CVE-2003-0543
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2003-10-01 | Updated: 2024-08-08 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 146: OpenSSL ASN.1 < 0.9.6j/0.9.7b - Brute Forcer for Parsing Bugs (dos/multiple, 2003-10-09, verified=1)

Integer overflow in OpenSSL 0.9.6 and 0.9.7 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via an SSL client certificate with certain ASN.1 tag values.
